newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia police chief orders security stepped up.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia police chief orders security stepped up.

text.p: Cambodia's police chief on Wednesday ordered security forces to step up vigilance and be prepared for terrorist threats following a rise in political tensions.

"Every unit of the police should increase protection, security and stability in society and prepare to fight against all kinds of terrorist threats that violate the people's rights and especially increase protection for politicians, the press, diplomats, etc," Hok Lundi said in a statement.

Tensions between the two parties in Cambodia's fragile ruling coalition have soared since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a protest led by Sam Rainsy, an opposition leader and ally of the royalist FUNCINPEC party.
Nineteen people were killed and more than 100 people were wounded in that attack.
First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC shares power in the coalition with the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) of Hun Sen. Both parties have loyal members in the police.

The deterioration in the political situation has been exacerbated this week by a bid by exiled former foreign minister Prince Norodom Sirivudh to return home more than a year after he was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment in absentia on charges linked to an alleged plot to assassinate Hun Sen.

The prince, the half-brother of Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk and uncle to Ranariddh, Sihanouk's son, is in Hong Kong but the two airlines serving the Phnom Penh-Hong Kong route will not allow him to board.

Hok Lundi, a CPP member whose statement was read on pro-CPP Bayon Radio, said police should take measures to confiscate weapons and stressed that police officials should not serve the interests of any one group or individual.
The police chief said police refusing to implement the order would be punished.
A CPP official said the statement was aimed at preparing the way for a statement by Hun Sen which could come on Thursday. He would not elaborate.

FUNCINPEC narrowly beat the incumbent CPP in U.N.-supervised elections in 1993, winning 58 seats against 51 for the CPP and 11 held by two smaller parties. The polls ended decades of war and internal strife in Cambodia.
On Tuesday, a senior royalist party member who is also a former comrade-in-arms of Hun Sen's, criticised Ranariddh's leadership, saying the co-premier's policies could lead Cambodia to disaster.
Minister of State Ung Phan urged other members of the FUNCINPEC party to endorse a statement "rejecting" the prince's authority. The CPP issued a statement backing Ung Phan's statement.
Ranariddh, who had left Cambodia on Monday, returned on Wednesday afternoon and was whisked under heavy security to preside over a meeting of the FUNCINPEC steering committee.
A party official said they would discuss expelling Ung Phan. He said the meeting would continue on Thursday.
